models_evaluated: commercially available AI algorithm for PI-RADS scoring and lesion detection on prostate mpMRI (unnamed)

links.outcome: AI versus radiologist sensitivity and specificity for csPCa on same MRI exams
links.effect: Patient level sensitivity/specificity 92%/64% radiologists vs 91%/57% AI; lesion level 90%/70% vs 81%/78% (PI-RADS ≥4). AI sensitivity comparable to radiologists.
links.quote: Sensitivity and specificity for clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa, defined as ISUP ≥ 2) were 92%/64% for radiologists vs. 91%/57% for AI detection on patient level and 90%/70% vs. 81%/78% on lesion level, respectively (cut-off PI-RADS ≥ 4).

links.outcome: csPCa cases missed by AI at patient level and negative predictive value
links.effect: Two csPCa cases missed by AI on patient level; NPV 0.88 at PI-RADS ≥3 cutoff.
links.quote: Two cases of csPCa were missed by the AI on patient-level, resulting in a negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.88 at a cut-off of PI-RADS ≥ 3.

screen.reason: Multicenter retrospective validation benchmarking diagnostic accuracy of a commercial AI tool against radiologists for prostate MRI.
